new_statements.quote: The accent in words of two syllables or more falls on the last syllable but one. In words of many syllables it commonly falls on the alternate ones reckoning backwards from the penultimate, or last syllable but one. So, Móna Mwána a mukwákwa a Ncémbi, (Behold the Lamb of God). But the earlier accents in long words are not sounded quite so heavily as the last accent. This is especially the case with tenses of verbs, and infixed pronouns.
new_statements.citation: Westcott, William Henry. n.d. [1923?]. Concise grammar of Luna Inkongo. Bristol: Henry Hill Limited, Printers.
new_statements.locator: Lesson 3, section 'ACCENTS', p. 13 (PDF page 8, right half); examples continue on p. 14
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary accent on the penultimate syllable of every word of two or more syllables; in longer words weaker accents fall on alternate syllables counting leftward from the penult (e.g. p. 14 Kátusóli, kísolélekýela, múkyeléngi).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Yes: 'the earlier accents in long words' fall on alternate syllables reckoning backwards from the penult and 'are not sounded quite so heavily as the last accent', especially in verb tense forms and with infixed pronouns; marked with acute accents in the p. 13-14 examples.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; 'commonly' hedges the alternating pattern. Missionary description with no phonetic instrumentation; tone is not mentioned anywhere in Lessons 1-3 (the language is presumably tonal like its Luban/Songe neighbours, so 'accent' here may conflate stress and penultimate lengthening).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('in words of two syllables or more'); illustrated in running sentences of the mission literature; verbs with tense prefixes and object infixes explicitly included.
new_statements.identity_note: Westcott describes the speech of Inkongo itself (the mission station on the Sankuru, 'Luna Inkongo'), which he says is the school/education standard of an area with 'many variations of dialect' wedged between Bakuba, Baluba and Batetela (Foreword, p. 3); he contrasts 'the Inkongo people proper' with 'the Luba people' (p. 10). Glottolog has no dialect nodes under luna1244, so the description is taken as the language-level luna1244.

sources.note: Lessons 1-3 (pp. 5-14) cover alphabet, vowels, consonants, syllable structure and pronunciation; a headed paragraph 'ACCENTS' on p. 13 states that accent falls on the penultimate syllable, with lighter alternating accents on preceding syllables in long words; accented example sentences on pp. 13-14.

Second-hand: 'Stress typically falls on the penultimate syllable' (unsourced sentence in a phonology section otherwise cited to Westcott 1923 pp. 5-6); supplies the biblafrique.net PDF URL for Westcott.
